simtte: Simulate Time-to-Event Data from PK/PD and Bespoke ODE Models

Source: R/simtte-package.R
simtte-package.Rd

Details

Simulates time-to-event (survival) datasets for clinical trial design and analysis, including datasets driven by a joint pharmacokinetic/pharmacodynamic (PK/PD) model solved via the mrgsolve backend.

Which functions go together

The usual chains: tte_model (or a name from sim_tte_ode_models) \(\to\) sim_tte_ode \(\to\) add_censoring and/or add_interval_censoring. For visit schedules: visit_schedule \(\to\) thin_visits or visit_schedule_informative \(\to\) add_interval_censoring. For the older closed-form path: sim_tte or sim_tte_df, with explore_pi_tq_surv for exploration. In parallel or multi-process runs, simtte_prepare_model wraps the model step on each worker.

Joint PK/PD and time-to-event simulation

sim_tte_ode locates each subject's event time directly during ODE integration ("in-solver" event detection): the survival probability is added to a PK/PD model as one more ODE compartment, p11, with dxdt_p11 = -p11 * HAZ, and the solver is watched for the first internal evaluation at which p11 falls to or below a per-subject uniform draw. Six built-in library models ("pk_hazard", "irm1_hazard"–"irm4_hazard", "tmdd_hazard"; sim_tte_ode_models lists all of them) cover common PK/PD structures out of the box. See vignette("pkpd-time-to-event", package = "simtte") for a full walkthrough.

Bring your own PK/PD model

tte_model converts any user-supplied mrgsolve model (one with an $ODE/$DES block) into one usable by sim_tte_ode the same way as a built-in model, including coexistence with a model's own declared $OMEGA block. See vignette("bring-your-own-model", package = "simtte").

Covariates, the linear predictor, and between-subject variability

sim_tte_ode's covariates/beta (optionally formula, built into a design matrix via model.matrix) add a linear predictor lp(t) = X(t) %*% beta to any model; omega adds log-normal between-subject variability on a model's own structural PK/PD parameters. See vignette("pkpd-time-to-event", package = "simtte").

Bespoke parametric/flexible hazard simulation

sim_tte/sim_tte_df are the original API: a unified interface for closed-form Weibull and flexible M-spline baseline hazards, plus a fully model-agnostic entry point (sim_tte_df()) for any already-simulated (ID, time, p11) trajectory from any source. Event times are generated by inverse transform sampling from the resulting cumulative hazard function (Bender et al. 2005), with an optional sub-grid refinement (event_time_method = "log_survival"). See vignette("introduction", package = "simtte").

Right censoring

add_censoring adds a second, independent censoring process to the output of any of the three simulation functions above: a per-subject censoring time drawn from an exponential, Weibull, uniform, lognormal, gamma, or user-supplied distribution, with the observed time becoming min(event time, censoring time, administrative end). censoring_rate_for solves for the distribution parameter giving a target censoring fraction; draw_censoring_times draws from the same kind of spec directly. sim_tte_ode also accepts a censoring argument that applies this automatically, inside its own seeded draw. See vignette("censoring-and-assessment", package = "simtte").

Interval censoring and visit schedules

add_interval_censoring maps an already-simulated (and, if applicable, already right-censored) outcome onto an interval (L, R], given a visit/assessment-time schedule – visit_schedule builds one with fixed spacing and optional per-subject jitter, thin_visits layers non-informative missed visits/dropout on top, and visit_schedule_informative layers a visit process that reacts to the simulated outcome. sim_tte_ode also accepts a visits argument that applies interval censoring automatically, always after any censoring. See vignette("censoring-and-assessment", package = "simtte").

Full mrgsolve import

Not narrowed to importFrom(): mrgsolve defines several of its own methods on base generics (as.data.frame, as.matrix, ...) via S4 setMethod()/exportMethods(), not plain S3 registration (confirmed directly: mrgsims is an S4 class, and as.data.frame.mrgsims is not found by .S3methods() even once mrgsolve's namespace is loaded). Narrowing this to importFrom(mrgsolve, mread, mrgsim, ...) was tried and broke as.data.frame(mrgsim(...)) dispatch under devtools::load_all() (.sim_surv_df()'s own as.data.frame(out) call, used by every sim_tte()/ sim_tte_df() call) – a full import() is what makes a dependency's S4 methods on base generics reliably dispatchable from the importing package's own code, not just its exported function names, so it is kept.

References

Bender R, Augustin T, Blettner M (2005). Generating survival times to simulate Cox proportional hazards models. Statistics in Medicine, 24(11), 1713-1723. doi:10.1002/sim.2059

Royston P, Parmar MKB (2002). Flexible parametric proportional-hazards and proportional-odds models for censored survival data, with application to prognostic modelling and estimation of treatment effects. Statistics in Medicine, 21(15), 2175-2197. doi:10.1002/sim.1203
